pr_body:
### What problem does this PR solve?

Issue Number: close https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/issues/25460

Problem Summary:

This fixes the following issues:
* Previously `ALTER USER` did not correctly skip the privilege check for modifying the currently connecter user.
* Modifying other users required the `SUPER` privilege (this can be lowered slightly in most cases, based on if the user has `SYSTEM_USER`)
* The SEM `RESTRICTED_USER_ADMIN` was not respected.
* `UPDATE` privilege on `mysql.user` was not an acceptable substitute for `CREATE USER`.

### What is changed and how it works?

What's Changed:

The `ALTER USER` statement now skips privilege checks when modifying the currently connected user.

Modifying a different user is relaxed to the `CREATE USER`, unless the user has the `SYSTEM_USER` dynamic privilege (MySQL compatible behavior).

Because in TiDB any non-restricted dynamic privilege is also satisfied by `SUPER` that means that altering super users requires `SYSTEM_USER or SUPER ` privilege.

### Related changes

- None

### Check List <!--REMOVE the items that are not applicable-->

Tests <!-- At least one of them must be included. -->

- Unit test (covered by existing test: `TestAlterUserStmt`)

Side effects

- None

### Release note <!-- bugfixes or new feature need a release note -->

- The `ALTER USER` statement now skips privilege checks when modifying the currently connected user. A new `SYSTEM_USER` privilege has been introduced to control if higher privilege users can be modified or dropped.

I made a mistake in my investigation; my root user was defined as `root@localhost` not `root@%` so the error was caused by a missing user. MySQL does has a mechanism to prevent users from being altered or dropped, which is the `SYSTEM_USER` dynamic privilege:

```sql
mysql [localhost:8024] {u1} ((none)) > drop user root@localhost;
ERROR 1227 (42000): Access denied; you need (at least one of) the SYSTEM_USER privilege(s) for this operation

mysql [localhost:8024] {u1} ((none)) > ALTER USER root@localhost REQUIRE SSL;
ERROR 1227 (42000): Access denied; you need (at least one of) the SYSTEM_USER privilege(s) for this operation
```

Hi @SunRunAway ,

```
mysql> select current_user();
+----------------+
| current_user() |
+----------------+
| root@%         |
+----------------+
1 row in set (0.00 sec)

...

mysql> ALTER USER 'cloudAdmin'@'%' IDENTIFIED BY 'password';  // this should be forbidden
Query OK, 0 rows affected (0.02 sec)

mysql> GRANT SYSTEM_USER ON *.* TO 'cloudAdmin'@'%';  // this should be forbidden
Query OK, 0 rows affected (0.02 sec)

mysql> GRANT SYSTEM_USER ON *.* TO 'root'@'%';  // this should be forbidden
Query OK, 0 rows affected (0.03 sec)
```
Just to confirm: the `ALTER` and `GRANT`s should be forbidden because of `RESTRICTED_USER_ADMIN`, right?

```
mysql> select current_user();
+----------------+
| current_user() |
+----------------+
| cloudAdmin@%   |
+----------------+
1 row in set (0.00 sec)

...

mysql> ALTER USER 'root'@'%' IDENTIFIED BY 'password1';  // this should be ok.
```
I think you can grant `CREATE USER` to `cloudAdmin`.

> I think you can grant `CREATE USER` to `cloudAdmin`.

I discussed some changes with @SunRunAway yesterday that I am working on now. MySQL accepts UpdatePriv on mysql.user as a substitute for `CREATE USER`. We currently allow this substitute for `CREATE USER` and `DROP USER` but not `ALTER USER`. I will add it.

For the other changes:

* Currently ALTER USER is not considering SEM's `RESTRICTED_USER_ADMIN` correctly (I'll fix it shortly).
* The case that a super user can allocate additional privileges to `CloudAdmin` is weird, but expected behavior (ad discussed)

It looks that `SUPER` is able to grant privileges for `RESTRICTED_USER_ADMIN` but cannot revoke privs. The permission of `GRANT` was not mentioned in the design/spec docs.

```
tidb> select @@tidb_enable_enhanced_security;
+---------------------------------+
| @@tidb_enable_enhanced_security |
+---------------------------------+
|                               1 |
+---------------------------------+
1 row in set (0.00 sec)

tidb> show grants for root\G
*************************** 1. row ***************************
Grants for root@%: GRANT Select,Insert,Update,Delete,Create,Drop,Process,References,Alter,Show Databases,Super,Execute,Index,Create User,Create Tablespace,Trigger,Create View,Show View,Create Role,Drop Role,CREATE TEMPORARY TABLES,LOCK TABLES,CREATE ROUTINE,ALTER ROUTINE,EVENT,RELOAD,FILE,REPLICATION CLIENT,REPLICATION SLAVE ON *.* TO 'root'@'%' WITH GRANT OPTION
1 row in set (0.00 sec)

tidb> show grants for cloudAdmin\G
*************************** 1. row ***************************
Grants for cloudAdmin@%: GRANT Process,SHUTDOWN,RELOAD ON *.* TO 'cloudAdmin'@'%'
*************************** 2. row ***************************
Grants for cloudAdmin@%: GRANT Select,Insert,Update ON mysql.* TO 'cloudAdmin'@'%'
*************************** 3. row ***************************
Grants for cloudAdmin@%: GRANT Select ON performance_schema.* TO 'cloudAdmin'@'%'
*************************** 4. row ***************************
Grants for cloudAdmin@%: GRANT Select ON information_schema.* TO 'cloudAdmin'@'%'
*************************** 5. row ***************************
Grants for cloudAdmin@%: GRANT BACKUP_ADMIN,RESTORE_ADMIN,SYSTEM_VARIABLES_ADMIN,RESTRICTED_VARIABLES_ADMIN,RESTRICTED_STATUS_ADMIN,RESTRICTED_CONNECTION_ADMIN,RESTRICTED_USER_ADMIN,RESTRICTED_TABLES_ADMIN ON *.* TO 'cloudAdmin'@'%'
5 rows in set (0.00 sec)

tidb> ALTER USER 'cloudAdmin'@'%' IDENTIFIED BY 'password';
ERROR 1227 (42000): Access denied; you need (at least one of) the RESTRICTED_USER_ADMIN privilege(s) for this operation

tidb> GRANT SYSTEM_USER ON *.* TO 'cloudAdmin'@'%';
Query OK, 0 rows affected (0.03 sec)

tidb> REVOKE SYSTEM_USER ON *.* FROM 'cloudAdmin'@'%';
ERROR 1227 (42000): Access denied; you need (at least one of) the RESTRICTED_USER_ADMIN privilege(s) for this operation
```

I think it looks fine but still would like to check if this is expected. @morgo @SunRunAway

> I think it looks fine but still would like to check if this is expected. @morgo @SunRunAway

Yes, that is what I meant by this comment:

> The case that a super user can allocate additional privileges to CloudAdmin is weird, but expected behavior (and discussed)

It is weird that someone can `GRANT` additional privileges to a restricted user, but they are `SUPER` and do have these privileges to be able to grant so it is not totally unreasonable.

But then the rule of `RESTRICTED_USER_ADMIN` is that `SUPER` is not enough to be able to modify this user's permission. There is no memory of where the permissions were allocated from, so even though that user has `SUPER` and allocated the privilege, they can't now revoke it.

We looked at how this works with `SYSTEM_USER` when making this choice. You can modify the permissions of system users if you have the ability to grant those privileges, even if you are not a `SYSTEM_USER` yourself.

issue_context.title: ALTER USER can't be used to change your own password
issue_context.body:
## Bug Report

Please answer these questions before submitting your issue. Thanks!

### 1. Minimal reproduce step (Required)

If I am the user `u1, the following statements should be identifcal:

```sql
SET PASSWORD = 'acdc';
ALTER USER u1 IDENTIFIED BY 'acdc';
```

### 2. What did you expect to see? (Required)

Either statement should change the password (no additional privileges required)

### 3. What did you see instead (Required)

ALTER USER requires the CREATE USER privilege, but it should not for modifying your own password.

### 4. What is your TiDB version? (Required)

```sql
mysql> SELECT tidb_version()\G
```
